title: Main-sequence height predicts CPV detections after period and color adjustment in 4,091 TESS rapid rotators
abstract: We test whether rotation and color can explain the reported rise in complex periodic variable (CPV) detections with height above the main sequence. We use the released sector 56 to 107 sample of 4,091 rapid rotators with 126 on-target CPV labels. A logistic model adjusted for period and color gives an odds ratio of 2.53 per magnitude of height, with a 95% interval of 2.05 to 3.14. Adding brightness, signal strength, sector count, crowding and earlier observation gives 2.90 (2.14 to 3.94). The association remains in low-RUWE, low-crowding and one-sector subsets, and after known objects are removed. A separate stratified comparison of height >2 mag with height <=1 mag gives a common odds ratio of 28.68 (10.07 to 81.69) in 2,435 stars. A spline fits height better than a linear log odds term (nominal p=0.012). These tests strengthen the conditional luminosity association. They do not measure causal age effects, intrinsic occurrence or material lifetime. Shared labels, incomplete selection, unknown detection efficiency, close companions and uncertain ages limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and repeat steps are included. External record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Joint detection rates and height odds ratios in the selected rapid-rotator sample. Intervals are conditional on source labels.
Conditional fitted curves show that a linear log odds height term is an approximation. The band gives a pointwise 95% spline interval.

citations.reason: Reuses three verified derived tables to test whether the height association remains after joint adjustment and stratification.
